script: Today I messed up. I was 27, my boyfriend was 40, and we were at the house. The landlord, who doubled as our roommate, had this weird rule: no noise past 7pm. He'd say, "I am sleeping in the living room, keep it down after seven." But I didn't even realize he was asking us to be quiet, not to leave. We'd be blasting music, arguing, laughing like we owned the place. He was like, "Turn it off, stay in your room." I didn't get it until the lights flicked off at 7:15 and the whole building fell silent. And that's how it all started. I'd been living there for two years, and it felt like a bad sitcom. My brain kept buzzing with the landlord's snarky comments. "You're louder than a drill." I'd just be like, "No jerks here, you're the one who's loud." But here's the thing, the mental toll was real. The house felt like a pressure cooker. I couldn't sleep, couldn't focus, and every night felt like a battle. If this didn't work, I'd lose everything—my sanity, my life, my dog's life. And that's how it all started. Finally, I had had it. I told the landlord, "We're leaving today." I'd been struggling for too long, and I didn't want to be that guy who caved.
